hook: Pour a glass of water on a sandy beach and it vanishes in seconds. Pour it on a clay ball field after a storm and it sits in a puddle for hours. The difference is the size of the particles, and it decides which crops a farm can grow, where a septic drain field can go and how much a field needs watering.

prereq.why: The A horizon is topsoil: humus mixed with minerals.
Humus forms when decomposers break down dead organisms.

options: Water carrying dissolved substances down through the soil
Wind lifting soil off a field
prereq.why: Leaching moves dissolved nutrients and minerals downward with water.

figure.caption: The soil texture triangle. Read the percent clay, silt and sand along the three sides; where the three lines meet is the soil's texture class. Loam, shaded, is a balanced mix.

chain.cause: Sand grains are large and clay particles are tiny
chain.effect: sand leaves large pores, clay leaves very many tiny pores

chain.cause: Water moves easily through large, connected pores
chain.effect: sandy soil has high permeability and drains fast

chain.cause: Tiny pores hold water tightly and pass it slowly
chain.effect: clay soil has high water-holding capacity but drains slowly and can lack air

chain.cause: Clay and humus hold nutrients that water would otherwise leach away
chain.effect: a loam with humus is fertile, holds water and still drains

ideas: Soil texture is the share of sand (largest), silt and clay (smallest) particles. The soil texture triangle turns the three percentages into a texture class.
Loam is a balanced mix (roughly 40% sand, 40% silt, 20% clay) that drains well yet holds water and nutrients.
Porosity is the share of soil volume that is pore space. Permeability is how easily water flows through: highest in sand, with large connected pores; lowest in clay, with tiny pores.
Water-holding capacity is how much water a soil can hold against gravity: highest in clay and soils rich in humus, lowest in sand.
Soil fertility is the soil's ability to supply nutrients. Clay and humus hold nutrients; pH controls whether roots can take them up (most crops prefer about 6 to 7).

misconception.wrong: Sand drains fast because it has more pore space than clay.
misconception.right: Clay usually has as much or more total pore space; its pores are just tiny. Sand drains fast because its pores are large and connected: that is permeability, not porosity.

summary: Soil texture, the share of sand, silt and clay, sets how soil behaves. Sand drains fast (high permeability) but holds little water or nutrients; clay holds water and nutrients but drains slowly; loam balances the two. The texture triangle reads a sample's class from its three percentages. Humus and a pH near 6 to 7 make soil more fertile.
